How sure can we be?: Not very sure, so treat this with care. Most of the new water (99%) is on farmland. Radar can't tell a flood from flooded rice fields, and on one farmland test our map and the other satellite's map disagreed almost completely.
What could be wrong?: These are estimates. Very wet fields can sometimes look like water. Some spots, like steep hillsides, can't be seen clearly and are left out. Some NISAR data used is Provisional quality; numbers may change when reprocessed. Most detected new water lies on cropland, where radar cannot separate a flood from irrigated or flooded paddies; on one cropland window our map and OPERA disagreed almost completely. This place and these dates have not been compared with OPERA: the method was compared on one lake window (Jul to Oct 2026, track 83) only.
Did the water go down anywhere?: Yes, about 449 hectares dried out, while 1,938 hectares went under water.
